chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar who said: A righteous servant, peace be upon him, narrated to me:

He said: I asked him about the Mutamatti' (one performing Hajj al-Tamattu') who has no sacrificial animal, and his fasting [of the ten days] was delayed until he departed [from Mecca], and he has no residence [in Mecca to stay and fast]. He said: 'He fasts three days on the journey, if he wishes; and if he wishes, he fasts ten days among his people [after returning].'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a Mutamatti' pilgrim who cannot offer a sacrifice and misses the ten-day fast before leaving Mecca?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the jurisprudential flexibility (*rukhas*) granted to pilgrims performing Hajj al-Tamattu' who face hardship in fulfilling the compensatory fasting (*dam*) obligation. It illustrates the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease, allowing the pilgrim to distribute the ten days of fasting either during the return journey or after settling in their hometown, thereby accommodating varying levels of travel fatigue and logistical constraints.
